clue.text: Striking workers show up without leader

parts.note: hands are manual workers, as in factory hands

indicators.note: the first letter of the word for show up is dropped, its head removed

parts.note: to show up is to come, arrive

explanation.surface: Workers on strike make their point by refusing to turn up, with no leader among them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Striking' looks like the workers' industrial action, but it is the definition: good-looking. 'without leader' drops the C of COME, leaving OME.
explanation.definitionFit: Striking looks are attractive and impressive, the same as good-looking.

clue.text: Ditch double act badly falling short

indicators.note: the shortened piece is written twice over
the last letter is cut off the word for act badly, so it stops short

parts.note: to act badly or over-theatrically is to ham

explanation.surface: A comedy double act performs poorly and its jokes fall flat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'falling short' cuts HAM to HA, and 'double' writes it twice. A ha-ha is a sunken ditch with a wall, used on country estates to fence livestock without spoiling the view.
explanation.definitionFit: A ha-ha is a sunk fence: a trench with one walled side bounding a park or garden.

clue.text: FA present head of training

parts.note: the present moment is now

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, here from training

explanation.surface: The Football Association presents its head of coaching.
explanation.walkthrough: FA looks like the Football Association, but here it is 'Fanny Adams', British slang for nothing at all; NOWT is northern English dialect for nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweet FA, short for Fanny Adams, is British slang meaning nothing, just like the dialect word for nothing.

clue.text: Publicity flyer with letters following

parts.note: a flyer here is not a leaflet but an aircraft pilot, and the letters trailing behind are the advertising message traced in smoke across the sky

explanation.surface: A promotional leaflet arrives with a stack of letters after it in the post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flyer' suggests a printed handbill; it is a pilot who spells out adverts in smoke.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilot who traces advertising words in smoke trails is literally writing on the sky for publicity.

clue.text: Capturing rook, a bad move may somehow work

indicators.note: the shuffled letters capture, hold inside them, the letter for the chess piece
somehow says the letters are put together in some unstated way, a rearrangement

parts.note: R is the chess notation for a rook

explanation.surface: A chess player takes a rook with a bad move that might still somehow come off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' leaves the rearranged letters (MADAMEBOVAY) unstated; 'Capturing' puts R inside them. The chess picture hides that 'work' is a literary work: Flaubert's novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Madame Bovary is Gustave Flaubert's novel, a literary work.

clue.text: Fool nervous about grabbing wife

indicators.note: grabbing means the turned word takes hold of the wife letter inside it
about means the word for nervous is turned round

parts.note: a nervous, shy person is timid

explanation.surface: A jittery fool clutches at his wife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns TIMID into DIMIT, and 'grabbing' puts W inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A fool is a stupid person, the same as a dimwit.

clue.text: Fury about new motorway y-it's legally targeting property

indicators.note: about means the word for fury goes around the new letter

parts.note: fury is anger, ire
M is the British motorway prefix, as in the M1

explanation.surface: Road rage over a new motorway turns into a legal dispute about land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts IRE around N, then M follows. In rem is Latin legal language for an action against a thing (property) rather than against a person. The 'y-' before it's is an OCR stray from a dash.
explanation.definitionFit: In law, an action in rem is directed at property itself rather than at a person.

clue.text: Jacket that keeps me warm in storm? Yes and no

definitions.text: Jacket that keeps me warm in storm? Yes and no

parts.words: Jacket that keeps me warm in storm? Yes and no
parts.note: the word does name a weatherproof jacket, so yes, but it is also a large square-rigged sailing ship that would carry you through a storm without warming you, so no

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether their coat will really keep them warm in bad weather.
explanation.walkthrough: The name is both a windproof jacket and a big merchant sailing ship, hence 'Yes and no'.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a windcheater-style jacket and also a large merchant sailing ship driven by the wind.

clue.text: Boy coming up with ideas?

parts.note: Theo is a boy's name
coming up means rising

explanation.surface: A young lad is full of bright ideas.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: Theo rising, a boy coming up, is someone coming up with ideas.
explanation.definitionFit: Theorising is forming ideas or theories, so coming up with ideas describes it.

clue.text: Cook who artificially coloured old jam

definitions.note: a jam is a tight spot or predicament, a noun like the answer

indicators.note: to cook is to tamper with or falsify, so the letters of who are rearranged

parts.note: artificially coloured hair or cloth has been dyed

explanation.surface: A cook who dyed some old jam to make it look fresher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cook' rearranges WHO to HOW. 'Cook' looks like a chef; it is the anagram signal. A how-d'ye-do is an old-fashioned word for a mess or awkward fix.
explanation.definitionFit: A how-d'ye-do is a dated term for an awkward predicament, a jam or fix.

clue.text: State fine with what church leaders did?

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencil leads
church leaders ran the Church of England, CE, so they ran CE

explanation.surface: A country is fine with how its bishops behaved.
explanation.walkthrough: CE is the Church of England; its leaders 'ran CE'.
explanation.definitionFit: France is a nation, and a state can mean a country with its own government.

clue.text: Countryman points with enthusiasm during ramble

parts.note: N and E are compass points, north and east

indicators.note: during says the enthusiasm word sits within the ramble word

parts.note: to ramble is to wander
zeal is enthusiasm

explanation.surface: A rural walker makes his points eagerly on a long ramble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Countryman' suggests a rural type; it means a native of a country. 'during' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A New Zealander is a native of a particular nation, a countryman in that sense.

clue.text: Military top brass?

parts.note: top brass suggests senior officers, but read literally it is the senior brass player of a regiment, the soldier in charge of its trumpets

explanation.surface: A question about the army's senior officers.
explanation.walkthrough: A trumpet-major was the chief trumpeter of a cavalry regiment; it is also the title of a Thomas Hardy novel.
explanation.definitionFit: A trumpet-major is the head trumpeter of a cavalry regiment, literally the leading brass player.

clue.text: Urchin finds fare for voyage

definitions.meaning: a sea urchin of the flat or heart-shaped kind, such as a sand dollar, also goes by this name
hard dry ship's bread eaten by sailors on long voyages, also called hardtack

explanation.surface: A street urchin finds food for a sea trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Urchin' suggests a street child; here it is the sea creature.
explanation.definitionFit: The term names both a flat sea urchin and the hard biscuit eaten aboard ship.

clue.text: Burn coke: a scattering left in it?

definitions.text: Burn coke: a scattering left in it?

indicators.note: in places the left letter inside the shuffled letters
scattering throws the letters of these words about into a new order

explanation.surface: Burning coke leaves a scattering of it behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scattering' rearranges the fodder into COABUNKER, split around the L that 'in' places. The whole clue also describes the store where fuel is kept, with a few bits left after burning.
explanation.definitionFit: A coal bunker is a storage bin for solid fuel, where a scattering of coke might be left.

clue.text: Stole on board extra-terrestrial ship

indicators.note: on board means the stole word is carried inside the alien letters

parts.note: ET is the abbreviation for extra-terrestrial, as in the film
a boa is a long fur or feather stole

explanation.surface: Someone steals aboard an alien spacecraft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stole' looks like the past tense of steal; it is the scarf, BOA. An E-boat was a German fast attack craft of the Second World War.
explanation.definitionFit: An E-boat was a German motor torpedo vessel, a type of ship.

clue.text: Weapons with kick killing hundreds ultimately

parts.note: a kick or thrill is a buzz
a killing, a large profit, is also a bomb, as in making a bomb

indicators.note: ultimately points to the last letter of hundreds

explanation.surface: Weapons with real impact killed hundreds in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'killing' looks violent but is a financial windfall, a bomb in British slang. Buzz bombs were German V-1 flying bombs.
explanation.definitionFit: Buzz bombs were V-1 flying bombs, pilotless weapons of the Second World War.

clue.text: Delivery securing wicket, England's first, in game

indicators.note: securing means the delivery word holds the wicket word inside it

parts.note: in cricket a delivery is a ball bowled
a wicket is a small gate

indicators.note: first takes the opening letter of England's

explanation.surface: A cricket delivery takes a wicket, England's first of the game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wicket' suggests cricket; here it is a wicket-gate. Bagatelle is a table game of rolling balls into holes.
explanation.definitionFit: Bagatelle is a board game in which small balls are struck into numbered holes.

clue.text: Variable novel set round grand London locality

indicators.note: set round means the rearranged letters are placed around the letter for grand
novel means new, so the letters of variable are made into a new arrangement

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for grand, a thousand pounds

explanation.surface: A variable novel is set around a grand area of London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' rearranges VARIABLE into BELRAVIA, and 'set round' puts G inside. Belgravia is a wealthy district of central London.
explanation.definitionFit: Belgravia is an affluent residential district of west-central London.

clue.text: Inexperienced driver may go on it

definitions.meaning: inexperienced means raw or new to something
in golf, a driver is a club, and the putting surface around the hole is where the ball ends up

explanation.surface: A learner driver may set off on the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'driver' suggests a motorist, but it is a golf club or golfer; the green is the closely mown area round the hole.
explanation.definitionFit: Green means raw and untrained, and also names the putting surface on a golf course.

clue.text: Slightly disheartened carrying burden — some do all night

indicators.note: carrying means the remaining outer letters hold the next pieces inside
disheartened removes the heart, the middle, of slightly, keeping its first and last letters

parts.note: to lumber someone is to burden them, and lumber is useless clutter
some of something is part of it

explanation.surface: Someone slightly downhearted is carrying a burden through a long night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disheartened' keeps the first and last letters of Slightly, and 'carrying' wraps them round the rest. 'do' is a party, not a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A do is a social event or party, and a slumber party is one that runs through the night.

clue.text: Stop over following opening of fishing in Scottish region

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the first piece stands above the rest

parts.note: to stop something is to ban it
F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter, from fishing

explanation.surface: A fishing ban is followed in part of Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: Banff is a town and historic county in north-east Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Banff is a former county in north-east Scotland, a Scottish region.

clue.text: Italian sparkler — fine round stone

indicators.note: round means the fine letters go around the stone abbreviation

parts.note: A1, written as AI, means first-rate or fine
ST is the abbreviation for stone, the British unit of weight

explanation.surface: A fine Italian gem set around a stone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sparkler' suggests a gem; it is sparkling wine. A1 is read with letters as AI.
explanation.definitionFit: Asti is a sparkling white wine from Piedmont in Italy.

clue.text: Cheated brother had news value regularly

indicators.note: regularly takes every second letter of news value

explanation.surface: A swindled sibling was regularly in the headlines.
explanation.walkthrough: In Genesis, Esau was cheated of his birthright and blessing by his twin brother Jacob.
explanation.definitionFit: Esau is the Biblical brother whom Jacob tricked out of his birthright and blessing.

clue.text: Mean to come in drunk in daylight

indicators.note: the answer comes in the run of letters of the words drunk in daylight

explanation.surface: It is nasty to arrive home drunk in broad daylight.
explanation.definitionFit: Mean in the sense of cruel or unpleasant is a synonym for unkind.

clue.text: Adores one complete story initially found among others

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Adores one complete story initially found among others (8)': I (one) + DO (complete) gives IDO, but no reading of 'story initially found among others' gives LISES; a word looks misread or missing.
annotationWithheld.clue: Adores one complete story initially found among others

clue.text: Time and again saving hour if being careful

indicators.note: saving means the two time letters keep the other pieces safe between them
and again says the time letter is written a second time

explanation.surface: Again and again, someone careful saves an hour if possible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Time and again' looks like the stock phrase for repeatedly; it is T, then T once more.
explanation.definitionFit: Thrift is economy with money, the quality of being careful in spending.

clue.text: Minister's no way to give out posh kneeler (4-4) 23,269 Solutic

indicators.note: no means the way letters are removed from the minister word

parts.note: a minister of religion is a priest
ST, short for street, is a way
to give out, stop working, is to die
U means upper-class, posh

explanation.surface: A clergyman refuses to hand out a fancy prayer stool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no' removes ST from PRIEST. A prie-dieu is a prayer desk with a ledge for kneeling. The trailing '23,269 Solutic (4-4)' is OCR spill from the page.
explanation.definitionFit: A prie-dieu is a kneeling desk for prayer, a kneeler.
